whatsHappening.background: Sudan's current crisis grew out of a failed transition after the 2019 revolution that ended Omar al-Bashir's dictatorship. Civilian hopes for democratic rule were undermined as the military kept power, and in 2021 SAF leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo carried out a coup together. Civilian unrest continued in 2022, and in April 2023 the SAF and RSF turned on each other and launched a war over control of the country.

parties.name: Sudanese Armed Forces
parties.description: The national military led by Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and one of the two main forces fighting for control.

parties.name: Rapid Support Forces
parties.description: A powerful military offshoot led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo and accused of major atrocities against civilians.

parties.name: Foreign Influence
parties.description: The Wagner Group and support linked to the UAE have deepened the rivalry at the center of Sudan's crisis.

timeline.description: Omar al-Bashir's dictatorship ends after a mass civilian revolution, but the military keeps power.
SAF and RSF leaders stage a coup together, and civilian unrest continues under brutal military rule.
The SAF and RSF break into open war over leadership of the country.

civilianImpact.experiences: The war has destabilized Sudan and turned it into the world's largest humanitarian crisis on multiple fronts. Around 90% of children have lost access to formal education, 21.2 million people face acute hunger, and 12 million people have been displaced from their homes. Sexual violence by armed forces has left a quarter of the population at risk of gender-based violence. The RSF has also been accused of pillaging, rape, ethnic cleansing, and besieging civilians.

howToHelp.summary: Support can fund food aid, protection services, health care, and emergency relief for displaced families. Public pressure also matters: one concrete advocacy action raised in Sudan solidarity campaigns is joining global efforts to boycott the UAE over its role in the conflict.
